forecasts.label: Interest payable

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Watford's auditors set out route back to a clean opinion by 2027/28 after four disclaimed years
news_drafts.lead:
Watford Borough Council's external auditors, Azets, expect the council to receive a clean opinion on its accounts for 2027/28 at the earliest, according to a "build back" report put to the Audit Committee on 30 September 2026. An external audit is an independent check on the council's accounts. For each of the four years from 2021/22 to 2024/25 the auditors issued a disclaimed opinion, meaning they could not form reasonable assurance on the accounts. The last clean opinion was for 2020/21.

Azets' indicative timeline has 2025/26 disclaimed again, 2026/27 modified ("except for", meaning the auditor has reservations on specific areas), and 2027/28 unmodified. That assumes all planned rebuild work is completed. The auditors assess the council as at the "higher end of the risk spectrum" for the exercise, citing multiple years of disclaimers, the volume of movements in its reserves (money set aside), weaknesses in controls, and changes in key staff and systems. They say this means extensive testing of income and spending over the disclaimed years.

Estimated rebuild fees are £418,640 across 2024/25 to 2026/27: £105,305 already agreed and charged for 2024/25, £194,774 for 2025/26 and £118,561 for 2026/27. The figure for 2027/28 is still to be confirmed. All of it needs approval from Public Sector Audit Appointments, the body that sets audit fees. Azets also requires the council to keep its finance function "sufficiently resourced" for both the annual audit and the rebuild testing.

The committee also had the council's treasury management report for 2025/26, covering how it borrows and invests spare cash. Interest paid on loans was £0.95m against a £1.41m budget, and investment income was £0.94m against £0.52m budgeted, though the 3.95% return trailed the 4.05% SONIA benchmark. The report says treasury activity met its limits "with limited exceptions"; it does not set them out in the main paper.

Internal auditors reported no new high-priority recommendations in 2026/27. Some earlier recommendations have slipped, among them a golf club governance review now due 30 October 2026.

findings.paper_title: Appendicies for Q1 Financial Monitoring Report ver 3
findings.headline: The council's risk register identifies high risk that the general fund balance will fall below its assessed minimum level.
findings.detail: Risk item Corp 7 is scored 12/16 (high risk: likelihood 3, impact 4) with the consequence that "the Council is unable to deliver commitments set out in the Corporate Delivery Plan" due to "the general fund balance falls below the risk assessed level." The register also flags government grant reduction (Risk 18, scored 12/16) and commercial income decline (Risk 15, also 12/16) as contributing pressures.
findings.matters: A council's general fund balance is its buffer against unexpected pressures. If the council's own assessment shows material risk of breaching the minimum level, it indicates the council is running with limited headroom for further economic deterioration or delivery slippage.
findings.figures: Risk Corp 7 scored 12/16 (likelihood 3, impact 4). Risks 18 and 15 also scored 12/16.
findings.quote: In that the general fund balance falls below the risk assessed level and the Council is unable to deliver commitments set out in the Corporate Delivery Plan. This appears as item no.7 on the Council's corporate risk register.

findings.paper_title: Appendicies for Q1 Financial Monitoring Report ver 3
findings.headline: The council identified £97,000 of centrally held efficiency savings that will not be delivered.
findings.detail: In the Corporate Costs budget line, the council has recorded an overspend of £97k with the explicit note that "Efficiency savings held centrally will not materialise." This represents a gap between planned savings and achieved savings, at a time when the risk register indicates concern about the general fund balance falling below assessed minimum levels.
findings.matters: Many councils rely on central contingency savings to bridge budget gaps. If Watford's savings assumptions are not holding, it signals tighter headroom than budgeted and may require further action to balance the year-end position.
findings.figures: £97k overspend in Corporate Costs budget line.
findings.quote: Efficiency savings held centrally will not materialise

findings.paper_title: Appendicies for Q1 Financial Monitoring Report ver 3
findings.headline: The council's investment property portfolio is delivering £292,000 less income than budgeted due to vacant units and tenants in administration.
findings.detail: Three major assets—Watford Business Park, Charter Place, and Intu Watford—are generating shortfalls of £172k, £60k, and £60k respectively. The shortfalls are driven by loss of rental income from vacant units and increased costs. The budgetary risk register explicitly identifies commercial rent income as a high-risk item (scored 12/16) with high likelihood (4), citing "tenants going into administration."
findings.matters: The risk register states that rental income is "a significant proportion of the total income the Council receives." If this represents a structural decline rather than cyclical vacancy, the council's medium-term income assumptions are at risk and may require reserve support or budget reduction.
findings.figures: Core Portfolio overspend £292k; Watford Business Park £172k, Charter Place £60k, Intu Watford £60k.
findings.quote: Net increase in costs on Watford Business Park due to loss of income from vacant units, rates and professional fees - £172K. Lower income from Charter Place due to vacant units, professional and utility costs - £60k. Drop in come from Intu Watford due to increase in fitout costs and loss in income from vacant units - £60k.

findings.paper_title: Appendicies for Q1 Financial Monitoring Report ver 3
findings.headline: Temporary accommodation numbers and costs are running 3% above forecast, with critical new build schemes now delayed.
findings.detail: At the end of Q1 (August 2026), TA households averaged 310 actual versus forecast of 298, with monthly B&B costs £40,000 above budget. The council's year-end forecast depends on lettings from Sydney Road (October, 24 lets), Northcott's (delayed to December), and Cygnet House/Plover House (delayed to February 2027). The report warns that if Sydney Road is delayed further, the forecast will need to be reviewed and costs could escalate materially.
findings.matters: TA demand is largely outside council control but consumes reserves if overspent. If new build delivery slips further, the council faces unbudgeted costs at a time when risk registers show general fund balance already at risk of falling below minimum levels.
findings.figures: 265 households at April 2026, 305 by August 2026; monthly cost forecast £232.5k vs actual £244k in August; assumes 24, 7, and 11 lets from three schemes.
findings.quote: Although TA numbers are currently running approximately 3% above forecast, the financial impact remains relatively small and may be absorbed later in the year as new build properties become available to let... If planned supply is delayed any further, a review of the year-end forecast may be required.

findings.paper_title: 202627 Financial Monitoring Report - Quarter 1 V9 Cabinet
findings.headline: Environment services delivered £0.764m underspend from pension contribution savings and SLM cost reductions, but the report suggests this may not be repeatable.
findings.detail: Environment achieved a significant underspend of £0.764m, with approximately £0.400m from reduced Veolia pension contributions following the 2025 triennial review, plus £0.200m from SLM pool management reductions and £0.100m from recycling efficiencies. However, triennial pension reviews and contract negotiations are not annual events, so this saving is unlikely to repeat at the same scale next year.
findings.matters: While positive for Q1, a finance director needs to understand which savings are recurring and which are one-offs. The £0.764m largely reflects non-repeatable pension and contract adjustments, not operational efficiency gains. The MTFS needs to reflect this correctly or the council could face a cliff-edge in 2027/28.
findings.figures: £0.764m Environment underspend: ~£0.400m pension contributions, ~£0.200m SLM costs, ~£0.100m recycling, ~£0.050m tendering.
findings.quote: There is a forecast underspend of (£0.764m) which is mainly due to approximately (£0.400m) savings on Veolia pension contributions. This saving resulted from the councils 2025 triennial pension review and proposed reductions in Pension contribution rates for the Veolia Environmental Maintenance Contract in 2025/26.
